jobs.prompt:
the post-launch node-first setup and manual capture flow

Implement the post-launch node-first setup and manual capture flow. Implement the specified post-launch contributor UX in source and local fixtures. When sign-in, viewer identity, permissions and binding are present, complete setup and explain first-install network participation, which defaults on with a clear persistent Settings opt-out. Keep ordinary authentication, user challenges, pricing, privacy and presence checks intact. Present one accessible primary manual capture action on supported search, account and lead pages, with clear states, progress and a distinct cancellation control. Arbitrate exclusive tab ownership before manual work, drain or cancel already-owned network work by the existing protocol, and suppress incoming network starts until manual settlement. Resume only if still eligible and opted in. Separate new-install default from durable preferences and preserve previous opt-outs on update, worker restart, popup reopen and ordinary refresh. Verify through the normal entry points. #16: Cover first install, incomplete setup prerequisites, all three supported synthetic page types, unsupported pages, simultaneous manual start/network wake, active network claim handoff, manual success/failure/cancel, and opt-out/re-enable across restart/update. Check the visible progress and accessible actions and that no fake worker executes two captures. Work in the extension source and its local tests. Use generated DOM fixtures, mocked browser/storage/transport APIs and fake clocks as appropriate. Keep verification offline and use fictional records. Do not contact any live service, use credentials or customer data, or operate a real account. Inspect current implementation before editing. Report the changed files, commands actually run, per-issue assertions and any unverified acceptance criteria.

Target issues: #16. Lead this issue group as gpt-6.2-astra at ultra effort. Use gpt-6.2-sol developers at max effort with separate file ownership and independent verification. Use the repository's normal local checks and generated synthetic fixtures. First inspect the current code and tests; when the base already satisfies an item, establish that directly. Retain existing fixes. For each numbered issue report its concrete behavior, tracked regression coverage and the exact commands and outcomes. Run the repository's complete affected test suites and update generated content hashes where required. Do not deploy, use production systems, change external settings or publish sensitive data. Finish on your result branch.

The owner has paused the Release 2 launch. Preserve today's shipping defaults. Make the post-launch flow available under an explicit, disabled-by-default release setting and verify it in offline fixtures. An ordinary install or update must retain existing behavior until a separate release decision. On current development fresh storage starts disabled, with automatic start permitted after a verified content-ready event; explicit Stop persists an opt-out. Establish both baseline behaviors in regression tests. Exercise the post-launch operations with the switch enabled only in synthetic fixtures, and the normal shipping entry points with the switch off. Do not roll out or publish anything.
